\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Fourier component on a coordinate set]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b003}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b012,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b014,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p216-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p217-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p218-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierComponentAtSupport, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ has one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and is orthonormal for
the inner product weighted by $\pi$. For a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ and a
set $S$ of coordinates, its orthogonal component at $S$ is the Fourier component of $f$
supported on $S$.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p209-b002}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$,
and a coordinate set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, its Fourier component supported on $S$
equals the sum, over all multi-indices $a\in\iota^n$ whose nonconstant coordinates are
exactly $S$, of its Fourier coefficient at $a$ times the product basis function
$x\mapsto\prod_{i=1}^n\psi_{a_i}(x_i)$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p216-b003}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a
function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, let its Fourier coefficient at a multi-index
$a\in\iota^n$ be its inner product with the corresponding product of basis functions,
and let its component on $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ be the sum of the terms whose
indices differ from the constant index exactly on $S$. The Fourier coefficient of this
component at $a$ equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if those indices differ from the
constant index exactly on $S$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Composition of coordinate projections]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_projectOnCoordinates}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_projectOnCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_projectOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and suppose
there is a finite nonempty index set $\iota$ and a basis of the real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner
product weighted by $\pi$. For any natural number $n$, any coordinate sets
$I,J\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and any $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, the successive
projections satisfy $P_I(P_Jf)=P_{I\cap J}f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier coefficient of a finite sum]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_finset_sum}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_finset_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_add, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2}
\difficulty{4}
Let $Ω$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $π$, and let $ι$ be a finite
nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions on $Ω$ that is
orthonormal for the $π$-weighted inner product and has a distinguished index $0_B$ whose
basis function is constantly one. For every $n\ge 0$, finite set $s$, family of
functions $f_k:Ω^n\to\mathbb R$ indexed by a type $κ$, and multi-index $a\inι^n$, the
Fourier coefficient of the sum of $f_k$ over $k\in s$ equals the sum of their Fourier
coefficients at $a$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner
product weighted by $\pi$. For any $n\in\mathbb N$, real-valued functions $f,g$ on
$\Omega^n$, and coordinate set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the Fourier component of
$f+g$ supported on $S$ is the sum of the Fourier components of $f$ and $g$ supported on
$S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal decomposition by coordinates]
\lean{FABL.IsOrthogonalDecomposition}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p218-b001}
\label{FABL.IsOrthogonalDecomposition}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $n$ be a
nonnegative integer, and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$. A family of functions
$f_S\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ indexed by subsets $S$ of the $n$ coordinates is an
orthogonal decomposition of $f$ if their sum is $f$, each $f_S$ depends only on the
coordinates in $S$, and, whenever $T$ is a proper subset of $S$, the product-space inner
product of $f_S$ with every function depending only on coordinates in $T$ is zero.
\end{definition}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b003}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a basis of the real-valued functions on $\Omega$, indexed by a finite nonempty set,
whose zero-indexed vector is constant one and whose vectors are orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For any nonnegative integer $n$ and any real-valued
function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, the components of $f$ obtained by grouping its product-basis
Fourier expansion according to the set of coordinates where the index is nonzero sum to
$f$. The component indexed by each coordinate set $S$ depends only on the coordinates in
$S$, and is orthogonal in the product probability inner product to every function
depending only on a set $T$ properly contained in $S$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Alternating sum over a Boolean interval]
\lean{FABL.sum_booleanMobius_interval}
\label{FABL.sum_booleanMobius_interval}
\leanok
\difficulty{6}
Let $A$ and $S$ be finite subsets of a type with decidable equality, and suppose
$A\subseteq S$. Then the sum over all subsets $J$ of $S$ that contain $A$ of
$(-1)^{|S|-|J|}$ is $1$ if $A=S$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$,
and $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the Fourier component supported on $S$ is
$\sum_{J\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|J|}P_Jf$, where $P_Jf$ is the function obtained by fixing
the coordinates in $J$ and averaging over all other coordinates using $\pi^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Projection of a support component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.projectOnCoordinates_orthogonalComponent}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.projectOnCoordinates_orthogonalComponent}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_ite, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_projectOnCoordinates, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
a finite nonempty index set carry an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on
$\mathcal{X}$ that includes the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of
coordinates, function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}^n$, and coordinate subsets $S,T$, projecting
the Fourier component of $f$ supported exactly on $S$ onto the coordinates in $T$ gives
that component if $S\subseteq T$, and gives the zero function otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Initial set of coordinates]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $t$, the first $t$ coordinates among $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$ are
the coordinates whose values are less than $t$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[No coordinates in an empty initial segment]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinates_zero}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinates_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the set of the first $0$ coordinates among $n$ coordinates
is empty.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[All coordinates in full dimension]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinates_dimension}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinates_dimension}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$, the set of the first $n$ coordinates among $n$ coordinates
is the full set of coordinates $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of initial coordinate sets]
\lean{FABL.firstCoordinates_mono}
\label{FABL.firstCoordinates_mono}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,s,t\in\mathbb{N}$ with $s\le t$. Among $n$ coordinates, the set of the first $s$
coordinates is contained in the set of the first $t$ coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal Doob martingale projection]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDoobMartingale}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b002}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDoobMartingale}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.firstCoordinates, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let a
finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ be orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product and contain the constant-one function. For a nonnegative
integer $n$, a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and a nonnegative integer $t$,
the orthogonal Doob martingale at time $t$ is the projection of $f$ onto functions
depending only on the first $t$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, any real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$,
and natural numbers $s\le t$, projecting the Doob martingale at time $t$ onto the first
$s$ coordinates gives the Doob martingale at time $s$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal Doob difference]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDoobDifference}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b002}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDoobDifference}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDoobMartingale, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a coordinate $t$, its orthogonal Doob difference is the function obtained
by subtracting the orthogonal Doob martingale at time $t$ from that at time $t+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Projection of a Doob difference vanishes]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.project_orthogonalDoobDifference_eq_zero}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b002}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, any real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$,
and any coordinate $t\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, projecting the difference between the Doob
martingale at time $t$ and at time $t-1$ onto the first $t-1$ coordinates gives the zero
function.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$,
and $t\in\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the difference between the conditional averages of $f$ given
the first $t+1$ and the first $t$ coordinates equals the sum of its Fourier components
supported on subsets of the first $t+1$ coordinates that are not contained among the
first $t$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal degree part]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDegreePart}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b003,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b006
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a natural number $k$, its orthogonal degree-$k$ part is the sum of its
orthogonal components over all subsets of the coordinates having cardinality exactly $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal weight at a degree]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalWeightAtDegree}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b005}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalWeightAtDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDegreePart, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a natural number $k$, the orthogonal weight at degree $k$ is the inner
product of its orthogonal degree-$k$ part with itself under the product probability measure.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal low-degree part]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalLowDegreePart}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b003,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b006
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p015-b014,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalLowDegreePart}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a natural number $k$, its orthogonal low-degree part is the sum of its
orthogonal components over all subsets of the coordinates having cardinality at most $k$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal weight above a degree]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalWeightAboveDegree}
\statementsource{lmn-constant-depth-fourier}{
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p004-b005,
  pdf-63759bd909d5-p009-b001
}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p018-b007,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p028-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p124-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p220-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalWeightAboveDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a natural number $k$, its orthogonal weight above degree $k$ is the sum,
over coordinate subsets of cardinality greater than $k$, of the squared norm of the
corresponding orthogonal component under the product probability measure.
\end{definition}

  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p210-b003}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability law $\pi$, and let $\iota$ be a
finite nonempty index set. Suppose $\Omega$ has a real orthonormal basis indexed by
$\iota$ under $\pi$, with one basis vector equal to the constant function $1$. For a
function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$, let its Fourier coefficient at a multi-index
$a\in\iota^n$ be its inner product with the corresponding product of basis functions.
The Fourier coefficient at $a$ of the sum of all support components of $f$ indexed by
subsets of size $k$ equals the coefficient of $f$ at $a$ if the number of coordinates
where $a$ differs from the constant index is $k$, and equals $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For any $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, the squared norm of the sum of Fourier components supported on
coordinate sets of size $k$ equals the sum of the squares of the Fourier coefficients
indexed by multi-indices with exactly $k$ nonconstant coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Orthogonal component inner product sum]

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p209-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$, indexed by $\iota$, is orthonormal for the inner product given by expectation
under $\pi$, and one designated basis vector is the constant-one function. For any
natural number $n$ and any real-valued functions $f,g$ on $\Omega^n$, their inner
product under the product probability measure is the sum, over all subsets $S$ of the
$n$ coordinates, of the inner products of their Fourier components supported on $S$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p207-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability distribution on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$
that is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one
function. For every natural number $n$, every function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and
every coordinate $i$, the influence of $f$ at $i$ equals the sum, over all subsets
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ containing $i$, of the squared product-space norm of the
orthogonal component of $f$ supported on $S$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p045-b002}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
a finite nonempty index set carry an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on
$\mathcal{X}$ that includes the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates
and function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}^n$, the total influence of $f$ equals $\sum_{k=0}^{n} k
W_k(f)$, where $W_k(f)$ is the squared norm of its degree-$k$ component under the
product measure.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b002}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$,
function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and subset $S$ of the coordinates, applying the
product noise operator with parameter $\rho$ to the orthogonal component of $f$ indexed
by $S$ gives $\rho^{|S|}$ times that component.
\end{theorem}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For $n\in\mathbb N$, a parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$, a
function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and a coordinate set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
applying the product noise operator to $f$ and then taking its Fourier component
supported on $S$ gives $\rho^{|S|}$ times the Fourier component of $f$ supported on $S$.
\end{theorem}

Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set with a distinguished constant basis vector.
Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on $\mathcal{X}$ is orthonormal for expectation
under $\pi$. For any number $n$ of coordinates, function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}^n$, and
noise parameter $\rho\in[0,1]$, its noise stability is $\sum_{k=0}^{n}\rho^k W_k(f)$,
where $W_k(f)$ is the squared norm of its degree-$k$ component under the product
measure.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Supremum norm on a finite product]
\lean{FABL.productSupNorm}
\label{FABL.productSupNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $n$ be a natural number, and let
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The product supremum norm of $f$ is the maximum of
$|f(x)|$ over all inputs $x\in\Omega^n$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Pointwise bound by the product supremum norm]
\lean{FABL.abs_le_productSupNorm}
\label{FABL.abs_le_productSupNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productSupNorm}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set and let $n$ be a natural number. For any
real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$ and any $x\in\Omega^n$, $|f(x)|$ is at most
the supremum of $|f|$ over $\Omega^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection sup norm bound]
\lean{FABL.abs_projectOnCoordinates_le_productSupNorm}
\label{FABL.abs_projectOnCoordinates_le_productSupNorm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.abs_le_productSupNorm, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_mono, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productSupNorm, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. For
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, define its coordinate projection at $x\in\Omega^n$ by
averaging $f$ over an independent uniform-product draw on the coordinates outside $J$,
while using $x$ on $J$. The absolute value of this projection at every $x$ is at most
$\max_{y\in\Omega^n}|f(y)|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on an orthogonal Fourier component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.abs_orthogonalComponent_le}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.abs_orthogonalComponent_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_eq_mobius, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.abs_projectOnCoordinates_le_productSupNorm, FABL.productSupNorm, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability measure $\pi$, and let
$\{\phi_a:a\in\iota\}$ be a finite orthonormal basis of real functions on $\Omega$ in
the $\pi$-weighted inner product, with a constant-one basis vector indexed by $0$. For
any nonnegative integer $n$, function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, subset
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and point $x\in\Omega^n$, the absolute value of the sum of
the product Fourier terms whose indices differ from $0$ exactly on $S$ is at most
$2^{|S|}\max_{y\in\Omega^n}|f(y)|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Supremum bound for a support component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productSupNorm_orthogonalComponent_le}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productSupNorm_orthogonalComponent_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.abs_orthogonalComponent_le, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productSupNorm}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
a finite nonempty index set carry an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on
$\mathcal{X}$ that includes the constant-one function. For any number $n$ of
coordinates, function $f$ on $\mathcal{X}^n$, and subset $S$ of the coordinate set, the
supremum norm of the Fourier component supported exactly on $S$ is at most $2^{|S|}$
times the supremum norm of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Restriction to a product coordinate]
\lean{FABL.restrictProductCoordinate}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p098-b004}
\label{FABL.restrictProductCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.replaceCoordinate}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f$ be a real-valued
function on strings in $\Omega$ of length $n$. For a coordinate $i$ and a state $a\in\Omega$,
restricting $f$ at coordinate $i$ by $a$ gives the function on the remaining coordinates
obtained by fixing coordinate $i$ to $a$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate restriction and coordinate dependence]
\lean{FABL.restrictProductCoordinate_dependsOnly}
\label{FABL.restrictProductCoordinate_dependsOnly}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.replaceCoordinate, FABL.restrictProductCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on $\Omega^n$ that depends only on the coordinates in
a finite set $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. For any coordinate $i$ and value
$\omega\in\Omega$, the function obtained by replacing coordinate $i$ of each input by
$\omega$ depends only on the coordinates in $S\setminus\{i\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection and coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.coordinateProjection_restrictProductCoordinate}
\label{FABL.coordinateProjection_restrictProductCoordinate}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.projectOnCoordinates, FABL.replaceCoordinate, FABL.restrictProductCoordinate}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on it, and let
$n$ be a natural number. For any real-valued function $f$ on $\Omega^n$, distinct
coordinates $i,j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, and value $a\in\Omega$, projecting $f$ by
averaging over all coordinates except $j$ commutes with fixing coordinate $i$ to $a$:
the two resulting functions on $\Omega^n$ are equal.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Restriction preserves the lower-support component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.restrictProductCoordinate_orthogonalComponent_eq}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.restrictProductCoordinate_orthogonalComponent_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.coordinateProjection_orthogonalComponent_eq_zero, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_coordinateProjection, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_eq_zero_of_dependsOnly, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_injective, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zero, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_dependsOnly, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.coordinateProjection, FABL.coordinateProjection_restrictProductCoordinate, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.restrictProductCoordinate, FABL.restrictProductCoordinate_dependsOnly}

Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, a function $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, a set
$S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, a coordinate $i\in S$, and a state $\omega\in\Omega$,
applying the orthogonal-component projection for $S\setminus\{i\}$ to the function
obtained by fixing coordinate $i$ of the orthogonal component for $S$ at $\omega$ leaves
that function unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Vanishing mean after coordinate restriction]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_restrict_orthogonalComponent_eq_zero}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productMean_restrict_orthogonalComponent_eq_zero}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.fourierCoeff_zeroMultiIndex, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.restrictProductCoordinate_orthogonalComponent_eq, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.productMean, FABL.restrictProductCoordinate}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let $B$
be a finite orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that contains the
constant-one function. For any number $n$ of coordinates, function
$f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, subset $S$ of the coordinates with $|S|\ge2$, coordinate
$i\in S$, and value $\omega\in\Omega$, the product mean of the orthogonal component of
$f$ indexed by $S$, with coordinate $i$ fixed to $\omega$, is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Permuting product coordinates]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductInput}
\label{FABL.permuteProductInput}
\leanok
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the
$n$ coordinate positions, and let $x\colon\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega$. The permuted input
has value $x(\sigma(i))$ at each coordinate $i$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Equivalence induced by coordinate permutation]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductInputEquiv}
\label{FABL.permuteProductInputEquiv}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.permuteProductInput}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of
the $n$ coordinate positions. Reindexing functions from those positions to $\Omega$ by
$i\mapsto\sigma(i)$ defines a bijection, whose inverse reindexes by $\sigma^{-1}$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Permuting the input of a function]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductFunction}
\label{FABL.permuteProductFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductInput}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the
$n$ coordinate positions, and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$. The function obtained
by permuting the input of $f$ sends $x$ to the value of $f$ at the input whose $i$th
coordinate is $x(\sigma(i))$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Inverse action on product functions]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductFunction_symm_apply}
\label{FABL.permuteProductFunction_symm_apply}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction, FABL.permuteProductInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a type, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the
$n$ coordinates, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$. Permuting the inputs of $f$ by
the inverse of $\sigma$ and then by $\sigma$ leaves $f$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Inverse action on product functions]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductFunction_apply_symm}
\label{FABL.permuteProductFunction_apply_symm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction, FABL.permuteProductInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a type, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the
$n$ coordinates, and let $f:(\mathrm{Fin}(n)\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$. Permuting the inputs of $f$ by
$\sigma$ and then by its inverse leaves $f$ unchanged.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Permutation invariance of product inputs]
\lean{FABL.productProbabilityPMF_permuteProductInput}
\label{FABL.productProbabilityPMF_permuteProductInput}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.permuteProductInput, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productProbabilityPMF_apply}
\difficulty{2}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$n$ be a natural number, and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the $n$ coordinate
indices. For every function $x$ from those indices to $\Omega$, the product distribution
of $n$ independent samples from $\pi$ assigns the same mass to $x$ and to the input
obtained by permuting its coordinates according to $\sigma$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Permutation invariance of product inner product]
\lean{FABL.productInner_permuteProductFunction}
\label{FABL.productInner_permuteProductFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction, FABL.permuteProductInput, FABL.permuteProductInputEquiv, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfInner, FABL.productInner, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.productProbabilityPMF_permuteProductInput}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $\pi$ be a
probability mass function on $\Omega$. For any permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$
coordinates and any functions $f,g:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, their product inner product
under the independent product distribution with marginal $\pi$ is unchanged when both
functions are composed with the same coordinate permutation.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate dependence under permutation]
\lean{FABL.permuteProductFunction_dependsOnly}
\label{FABL.permuteProductFunction_dependsOnly}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a type, let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\sigma$ be a permutation of the
$n$ coordinates, and let $S$ be a finite set of coordinates. If a real-valued function
on $\Omega$-valued inputs depends only on the coordinates in $S$, then the function
obtained by permuting its inputs by $\sigma$ depends only on the coordinates in $\sigma(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Symmetry under coordinate permutations]
\lean{FABL.IsProductSymmetric}
\label{FABL.IsProductSymmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction}
Let $\Omega$ be a set, let $n$ be a natural number, and let $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb
R$. The function $f$ is invariant under coordinate permutations if, for every
permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ coordinate positions, evaluating $f$ after reindexing
its input by $i\mapsto\sigma(i)$ gives the same function $f$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Permutation of a symmetric function's Fourier component]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.permuteProductFunction_orthogonalComponent_of_symmetric}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.permuteProductFunction_orthogonalComponent_of_symmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.DependsOnlyOnCoordinates, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_dependsOnly, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalDecomposition_unique, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productInner_orthogonalComponent_eq_zero_of_ssubset, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.sum_orthogonalComponent, FABL.IsOrthogonalDecomposition, FABL.IsProductSymmetric, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.permuteProductFunction, FABL.permuteProductFunction_dependsOnly, FABL.permuteProductFunction_symm_apply, FABL.permuteProductInput, FABL.productInner_permuteProductFunction}

Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be an orthonormal basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one vector is indexed by a distinguished element of a finite nonempty index
set. For a function $f:(\Omega^n)\to\mathbb R$ invariant under every permutation of its
$n$ coordinates, every permutation $\sigma$ of those coordinates, and every subset $S$
of the coordinate set, permuting the input of the Fourier component of $f$ whose indices
are nonconstant exactly on $S$ yields the Fourier component whose indices are
nonconstant exactly on $\sigma(S)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Equal-degree component energies under symmetry]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_energy_eq_of_symmetric_of_card_eq}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_energy_eq_of_symmetric_of_card_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.permuteProductFunction_orthogonalComponent_of_symmetric, FABL.IsProductSymmetric, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner, FABL.productInner_permuteProductFunction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the
$\pi$-weighted inner product. For any $n\in\mathbb N$, suppose $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$
is invariant under every permutation of its $n$ coordinates. If
$S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ have the same cardinality, then the Fourier components of
$f$ supported on $S$ and $T$ have equal squared norms in the product measure $\pi^n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Empty support and the zero multi-index]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.multiIndexSupport_eq_empty_iff}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.multiIndexSupport_eq_empty_iff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.zeroMultiIndex, FABL.MultiIndex, FABL.multiIndexSupport}
\difficulty{4}
Let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis with distinguished index $0_B$, and let
$a:	ext{Fin}(n)\to\iota$ be a multi-index. Its support, the set of coordinates $i$ for
which $a(i)\ne 0_B$, is empty if and only if $a(i)=0_B$ for every coordinate $i$, that
is, $a$ is the zero multi-index.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Orthogonal component energy]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.productInner}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let a
finite nonempty index set label a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ that is
orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and contains the constant-one function.
For a nonnegative integer $n$, a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$, and a
coordinate subset $S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, the orthogonal component energy is the
product-measure inner product of the orthogonal component of $f$ associated with $S$
with itself.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegative component energy]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy_nonneg}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.pmfInner_self_nonneg}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $(\psi_a)_{a\in\iota}$ be a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$ that contains the constant-one function and is orthonormal for the inner
product weighted by $\pi$. For any $n\in\mathbb N$, any real-valued function $f$ on
$\Omega^n$, and any set of coordinates $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the squared norm of
the Fourier component of $f$ supported on $S$, with respect to the product probability
measure $\pi^n$, is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Size of the initial coordinate set]
\lean{FABL.card_firstCoordinates}
\label{FABL.card_firstCoordinates}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.firstCoordinates}
\difficulty{1}
If $k$ and $n$ are natural numbers with $k\leq n$, then the set of the first $k$
coordinates among $n$ coordinates has cardinality $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Symmetric level energy]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p122-b002
}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.firstCoordinates}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose a basis of real-valued functions on
$\Omega$ is orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$ and contains the constant-one
function at a distinguished index. For a function $f$ on $\Omega$-valued strings of
length $n$ and a natural number $k$, the symmetric level energy is zero when $k$ is zero;
otherwise it is the orthogonal component energy on the first $k$ coordinates.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Nonnegativity of symmetric level energy]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy_nonneg}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy_nonneg}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy_nonneg, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy, FABL.ProductL2}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, and let
$\iota$ be a finite nonempty index set. Suppose $B$ is a basis of real-valued functions
on $\Omega$, with one basis vector equal to the constant-one function and with the basis
orthonormal for expectation under $\pi$. For every natural number $n$, every function
$f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$, and every natural number $k$, the symmetric level energy of
$f$ at level $k$ is nonnegative.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Symmetric energy over a powerset]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.sum_energy_powerset_eq_sum_choose_levelEnergy}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.sum_energy_powerset_eq_sum_choose_levelEnergy}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponentEnergy, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_energy_eq_of_symmetric_of_card_eq, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy, FABL.IsProductSymmetric, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.card_firstCoordinates, FABL.firstCoordinates}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ and $\iota$ be finite nonempty sets, let $\pi$ be a probability mass
function on $\Omega$, and let $B$ be a basis of real-valued functions on $\Omega$ whose
constant-one element is indexed by $0$ and which is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted
inner product. For a positive integer $n$, let $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb R$ be invariant
under every permutation of its coordinates, and let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$. The sum
of the energies of the orthogonal components indexed by the nonempty subsets of $S$
equals $\sum_{k=0}^{|S|}\binom{|S|}{k} E_k$, where $E_0=0$ and, for $k>0$, $E_k$ is the
energy of the component indexed by the first $k$ coordinates.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of normalized projected variance]
\lean{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.normalized_projectedVariance_mono_of_symmetric}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b007}
\label{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.normalized_projectedVariance_mono_of_symmetric}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productVariance_projectOnCoordinates_eq_sum_energy, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.sum_energy_powerset_eq_sum_choose_levelEnergy, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.symmetricLevelEnergy_nonneg, FABL.IsProductSymmetric, FABL.ProductL2, FABL.mul_choose_le_mul_choose_of_le, FABL.productVariance, FABL.projectOnCoordinates}
\difficulty{5}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set, let $\pi$ be a probability mass function on
$\Omega$, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis for real-valued functions on $\Omega$,
indexed by a finite nonempty set. For $n\ge 0$, suppose $f:\Omega^n\to\mathbb{R}$ is
invariant under every permutation of its coordinates, and let
$S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfy $1\le |S|\le |T|$. Then the variance, under the
product probability measure with marginal $\pi$, of the conditional expectation of $f$
given the coordinates in $S$, divided by $|S|$, is at most the corresponding variance
for $T$ divided by $|T|$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Uniform expectation of a point indicator]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_threePointCIndicator}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_threePointCIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ThreePoint, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.threePointBasis, FABL.threePointCIndicator, FABL.threePointCIndicatorCoeff, FABL.threePointCIndicator_coefficient, FABL.threePointFourierFunction, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\{a,b,c\}$ be a set of three elements with the uniform probability distribution,
and let the indicator of $c$ equal $1$ at $c$ and $0$ at the other two elements. Its
expectation is $1/3$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coordinate projection of a three-point indicator]
\lean{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_threePointBothCIndicator}
\label{FABL.projectOnCoordinates_threePointBothCIndicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ThreePoint, FABL.mergeOnCoordinates, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_independentProductPMF_prod, FABL.pmfExpectation_threePointCIndicator, FABL.productProbabilityPMF, FABL.projectOnCoordinates, FABL.threePointBothCIndicator, FABL.threePointCIndicator, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{5}
Let $J\subseteq\{0,1\}$ and let $x:\{0,1\}\to\{a,b,c\}$. Under the product of the
uniform distributions on $\{a,b,c\}$, average the indicator that both coordinates equal
$c$, while keeping the coordinates in $J$ fixed at $x$. The resulting value is
$\prod_{i=0}^{1}\bigl(\mathbf{1}_{i\in J}\mathbf{1}_{x(i)=c}+(1-\mathbf{1}_{i\in
J})/3\bigr)$, where each indicator is $1$ when its condition holds and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Three point singleton value]
\lean{FABL.threePointSingletonOrthogonalValue}
\label{FABL.threePointSingletonOrthogonalValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ThreePoint}
Let $x\colon\{0,1\}\to\{a,b,c\}$ and choose $i\in\{0,1\}$. The singleton value at $i$ is
$2/9$ if $x(i)=c$, and is $-1/9$ otherwise.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Three point pair value]
\lean{FABL.threePointPairOrthogonalValue}
\label{FABL.threePointPairOrthogonalValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.ThreePoint}
Let $x\colon\{0,1\}\to\{a,b,c\}$. The pair value is $4/9$ if both coordinates equal $c$,
is $-2/9$ if at least one coordinate equals $c$ but they do not both equal $c$, and is
$1/9$ if neither coordinate equals $c$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Constant component of the two-coordinate indicator]
\lean{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_empty}
\label{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_empty}

\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_eq_mobius, FABL.projectOnCoordinates_threePointBothCIndicator, FABL.threePointBothCIndicator, FABL.threePointFourierBasis}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g$ be the indicator of $c$ on the equally weighted set $\{a,b,c\}$, and let
$f(x_0,x_1)=g(x_0)g(x_1)$. The Fourier component of $f$ supported on the empty set of
coordinates is the constant function with value $1/9$.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_singleton}

\begin{theorem}[Pair Fourier component]
\lean{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_pair}
\label{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_pair}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier formula for each support component]
\lean{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_fourier}
\label{FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_orthogonalComponent_fourier}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.orthogonalComponent_eq_fourierComponentAtSupport, FABL.FiniteFourierBasis.productFunction, FABL.multiIndexSupport, FABL.threePointBothCIndicator, FABL.threePointBothCIndicator_fourierCoeff_table, FABL.threePointCIndicatorCoeff, FABL.threePointFourierBasis}
\difficulty{3}
Let $g$ be the indicator of $c$ on the equally weighted set $\{a,b,c\}$, with Fourier
coefficients $\widehat g(0)=1/3$, $\widehat g(1)=-\sqrt2/6$, and $\widehat
g(2)=-\sqrt6/6$. For any subset $S\subseteq\{0,1\}$, the Fourier component of
$(x_0,x_1)\mapsto g(x_0)g(x_1)$ supported on $S$ is the sum, over pairs of indices
$(a_0,a_1)\in\{0,1,2\}^2$ whose nonzero-index coordinates are exactly $S$, of
\[\widehat g(a_0)\widehat g(a_1)\,\phi_{a_0}(x_0)\phi_{a_1}(x_1),\]
where $\phi_0,\phi_1,\phi_2$ are the three-point orthonormal Fourier basis functions.
\end{theorem}
